I can use current scroll identity and avoid stale proxy capture.
I can distinguish input focus, software keyboard visibility, and accessibility focus.

lessons.title: Forms: keyboards, editing ranges, validation, and localized input
lessons.summary: Preserve real editing behavior through typing, paste, AutoFill, IME composition, keyboard avoidance, focus progression, and domain validation.
objectives: Distinguish raw editing buffers, normalized domain values, and submission eligibility.
Configure keyboard traits without treating them as validators.
Convert UIKit NSRange edits correctly and preserve marked text and selection.
Provide keyboard-visible, hardware-keyboard, and accessible error recovery.
Audit the active address form's local normalization rules without claiming global address support.

sections.title: A text field owns an editing interaction, not just a String
sections.html:
An Android engineer may start with EditText filters or a Compose value/onValueChange pair. The important iOS distinction is between the editing buffer, the normalized domain value, and the value allowed to submit. A person can be midway through entering a number, composing a character, replacing a selection, or accepting AutoFill. The intermediate text can be temporarily invalid while still representing a valid editing action. Do not force every keystroke into the final serialized format if that makes ordinary input impossible.

TextField bound to String stores an editable string. A formatter-based or format-style field can parse typed values, but that introduces parsing and incomplete-input behavior you must understand. A blank decimal, a sign without digits, and a locale-specific separator are reasonable intermediate states. For many forms, keep raw strings and derive a parsed optional value for eligibility. Validation at the action boundary then constructs a domain request or reports a recoverable error. Keyboard input and network validation remain separate responsibilities.

Session 009's single-source rule still applies: a parent and child should not maintain independent copies of the same text synchronized by competing change callbacks. A UIKit representable may need additional editing metadata such as selectedTextRange and markedTextRange, but that does not justify creating a second business draft. State should survive an unrelated render, keyboard dismissal, and return from a detail. A live server error should not reassign identical text and throw the caret to the end. Start with those observable interaction requirements before choosing property wrappers or formatters.

sections.title: Keyboard type, content type, capitalization, and submit labels
sections.html:
keyboardType chooses an input presentation, such as emailAddress, numberPad, or decimalPad. It does not enforce an allowed character set. Paste, AutoFill, hardware keyboards, accessibility input, and programmatic updates can supply different text. A number-pad field therefore still needs the domain's numeric policy. Postal codes should normally be strings: converting a demo code such as 01234 to Int loses its leading zero. Whether only five ASCII digits are permitted is a local business rule, not an international postal-address rule.

textContentType supplies semantic hints for system-assisted input, such as givenName, emailAddress, postalCode, or oneTimeCode. Use the actual meaning, not whichever hint seems to produce a convenient keyboard. Capitalization and autocorrection are also interaction choices. A person's name is not safely normalized by rejecting all non-Latin letters or forcing a culturally assumed casing rule. SecureField changes secure entry behavior; do not casually toggle identity to reveal text because that can affect focus and selection. Credential-specific autofill requires additional focused study.

submitLabel changes the semantic label of an available submit key; it does not manufacture a Return key on every keyboard. A number pad often lacks one, so provide an explicit Done or Continue path, such as a keyboard toolbar or an always-reachable control. onSubmit can advance to the next unique focus case or validate the final form. A hardware keyboard should have a sensible route too. UIKit exposes corresponding UITextInputTraits and returnKeyType, but their implementation is not simply an Android imeOptions bitmask. Test behavior rather than only the requested trait values.

sections.title: Read a raw-buffer form with a declared synthetic rule
sections.html:
This self-contained SwiftUI example requires iOS 17 for the lesson's target baseline. It uses a display name and a synthetic five-ASCII-digit demo code. The rule is intentionally narrow and does not claim email, patient-name, or international-address validation.

import Foundation
import SwiftUI

struct DemoCodeForm: View {
    enum Field: Hashable { case name, code }
    @State private var name = ""
    @State private var code = ""
    @State private var attempted = false
    @State private var status = ""
    @FocusState private var focused: Field?

    private var validName: Bool {
        !name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty
    }
    private var validCode: Bool {
        code.utf8.count == 5 && code.utf8.allSatisfy { $0 >= 48 && $0 <= 57 }
    }

    var body: some View {
        Form {
            TextField("Demo display name", text: $name)
                .focused($focused, equals: .name)
                .submitLabel(.next)
                .onSubmit { focused = .code }
            TextField("Five-digit demo code", text: $code)
                .keyboardType(.numberPad)
                .textInputAutocapitalization(.never)
                .autocorrectionDisabled()
                .focused($focused, equals: .code)
                .submitLabel(.done)
                .onSubmit { submit() }
            if attempted && (!validName || !validCode) {
                Text("Enter a name and exactly five ASCII digits.")
                    .foregroundStyle(.red)
            }
            Button("Check demo input") { submit() }
            Text(status)
        }
        .toolbar {
            ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .keyboard) {
                Spacer()
                Button("Done") { focused = nil }
            }
        }
    }

    private func submit() {
        attempted = true
        guard validName && validCode else {
            status = ""
            focused = validName ? .code : .name
            return
        }
        focused = nil
        status = "Synthetic input is valid; nothing was submitted."
    }
}

$name and $code project bindings to their owned buffers. utf8 examines bytes, and the comparisons 48 through 57 explicitly choose ASCII digits. That differs from String.count and Unicode numeric predicates. allSatisfy alone would accept an empty sequence vacuously, so the exact count also matters. guard exits the invalid action path and chooses the first invalid field. The button is deliberately usable while invalid so the learner can receive feedback; merely disabling it would not explain what needs repair.

The keyboard toolbar clears focus without modifying either buffer. Error text is readable information, not only a red outline. A production form would add localized field-specific messages, server results, accessible error discovery, and a deliberate committed-value construction. This scratch status explicitly states that no request occurred.

sections.title: UIKit edit ranges use UTF-16; Swift strings use grapheme-aware indices
sections.html:
UITextFieldDelegate's shouldChangeCharactersIn range is an NSRange in the text's UTF-16 representation. Swift String.Index is not an integer character offset. Emoji, combining marks, and some scripts make naive range.location arithmetic incorrect. Convert the Foundation range with Range(range, in: currentText), which can fail if the range cannot be represented correctly. Build the proposed buffer by replacing that Swift range with the entire replacement string. Deletion, paste, and selected replacement can involve more than one character.

import Foundation

func replacingDemoText(_ current: String, range: NSRange, replacement: String) -> String? {
    guard let swiftRange = Range(range, in: current) else { return nil }
    return current.replacingCharacters(in: swiftRange, with: replacement)
}

The question mark in String? represents a failed conversion honestly; guard unwraps the successful range. A replacement of the emoji in A🙂B uses UTF-16 location 1 and length 2, even though the emoji is one Swift Character. Do not slice a String using those numbers as character positions or assume NSString.length and String.count describe the same unit. Successful conversion also does not certify that a fabricated range respects grapheme boundaries. Use ranges supplied by the text system; if your domain requires whole-Character boundaries, validate them separately against the string's allowed indices. An out-of-bounds range can return nil, but a range through part of a surrogate pair must not be assumed to fail conversion.

markedTextRange identifies provisional text used by input methods during composition. Aggressively uppercasing, truncating, or rewriting the whole buffer while marked text exists can break composition and selection. A raw-buffer design can permit provisional edits, then validate or normalize at a declared commit/submission boundary. If a bridge must transform committed text, preserve or deliberately remap the caret and selection, and avoid reassigning an identical value in updateUIView. onChange of a String alone does not expose every input-method detail; choose a UIKit bridge only when the interaction contract needs that control, and test actual composition.

sections.title: Keyboard avoidance needs the current container and one owner
sections.html:
A form should keep the active field and its recovery actions reachable while the keyboard is visible. SwiftUI's normal safe-area and scroll behavior often supplies a useful starting point. A ScrollView or Form can scroll long content; safeAreaInset can place a bottom action while preserving scrollable space. ignoresSafeArea(.keyboard) changes that negotiation and can defeat avoidance. Do not add a global keyboard-height observer simply because an old Android implementation manually applied insets.

UIKit's keyboardLayoutGuide gives constraint relationships from iOS 15, and scroll integration may need content inset adjustment plus scrolling the active control into view. If using keyboard notifications, their frames are in a screen coordinate space: convert into the actual window/view and use intersection with the visible region. Subtracting the raw reported height from every form fails for floating keyboards, multiple windows, and nested containers. Hardware keyboards can change focus without the same software-keyboard geometry, so do not treat keyboard visibility as an editing-lifetime signal.

Focus progression needs distinct field identities, as session 032 showed. Advancing when two letters appear may help one fixed state-code field, but can surprise users replacing text or accepting AutoFill. Keep an explicit next/submit route, and inspect the exact rule before copying auto-advance. Clearing focus should leave raw buffers intact. A server error arriving during editing should not rebuild the hosted form or replace its state identity. For dismissal and navigation return, document whether the previous field refocuses; avoid arbitrary sleeps as proof the responder hierarchy is ready.

sections.title: Validation, normalization, and localization have separate contracts
sections.html:
Normalize only what the domain permits. Trimming outer whitespace can be appropriate for submission eligibility without altering internal spacing while typing. Case-folding an email address, accepting Unicode decimal digits, or stripping punctuation from a code needs a specified policy. Regex can check a bounded format, but does not prove an email inbox exists or an address is deliverable. Server validation may add facts the client cannot know; keep its failure recoverable and preserve the user's draft.

When async validation depends on current text, tag the request with the input revision and reject obsolete success and error results. A delayed answer for an earlier address must not mark the edited address invalid. Decide when errors appear: after blur, after first submit, or during input once correction becomes useful. A hidden disabled Continue action without a reason is weak feedback. Report field-specific errors near their control and consider VoiceOver discovery or an appropriate accessibility announcement without repeatedly interrupting every keystroke.

Localized strings need room to grow and semantic labels that remain after a placeholder disappears. Number and date entry must use the chosen locale and domain format rather than an assumed period separator or month/day order. Right-to-left layouts need leading/trailing relationships and inspection of mixed-direction text. String length rules should name their unit: bytes, UTF-16 units, Unicode scalars, or grapheme clusters. An ASCII code contract can count bytes; a display-name limit usually needs a different policy. International address schemas, bidirectional-text editing, and locale-aware numeric parsing deserve specialist exercises rather than a claim that this one form covers them.

sections.title: Audit the active address form without generalizing its local rules
sections.html:
BookingAddressFormView binds its observable model, defines one optional FocusState, assigns semantic address content types, advances on submit, and uses a number pad for ZIP. The model clamps field lengths, uppercases or maps recognized state names to USPS abbreviations, and derives currentAddress by trimming and converting empty strings to nil. These are local address assumptions. The source's digitsOnly uses Character.isWholeNumber, which is broader than ASCII 0–9; do not describe it as an ASCII-only validator or claim it proves backend acceptance of every Unicode digit.

display(address:) temporarily suppresses delegate notifications during batch prefill. setError guards identical writes because the surrounding booking controller repeatedly reevaluates validity while typing. That is a concrete example of separating programmatic population from user-edit events and limiting unnecessary observed updates. The course's scratch form intentionally avoids rewriting every keystroke; it is a teaching contract, not a claim that the production normalization strategy has been migrated or universally handles IME composition.

The older UIKit BookingTextField also adjusts editing and placeholder rectangles as text scales. Correct buffers alone do not prove readable input, and correctly sized fields alone do not prove cursor or AutoFill behavior. Acceptance evidence should include paste with a selection, deletion, a leading-zero code, non-ASCII input, composition on an actual input method, and keyboard-visible error recovery. Automated model tests can prove format rules; device interaction is needed for responder, input-method, and keyboard behavior. Read the active tests as a coverage starting point, while leaving unrun client checks and specialist internationalization review explicit.

quiz.question: A number-pad field receives pasted letters. Which conclusion is correct?
options: UIKit cannot accept paste into a number-pad field.
Keyboard type is a presentation hint; the domain still validates the buffer.
The value is automatically converted to Int.
quiz.explanation: Paste, AutoFill, hardware input, and programmatic writes are not restricted by the visible keyboard. The action must enforce the actual domain format.

quiz.question: How should shouldChangeCharactersIn's NSRange be applied to a Swift String?
options: Use range.location directly as a String character index.
Assume range.length is always one.
Convert using Range(range, in: current), handle failure, then replace that range.
quiz.explanation: UIKit supplies UTF-16 ranges, while Swift string indexing respects variable-width representations. Conversion is necessary for emoji and other nontrivial text.

quiz.question: Why avoid rewriting the whole buffer during marked text?
options: It can disrupt provisional input-method composition and selection.
Marked text is already persisted to disk.
All marked text is invalid user input.
quiz.explanation: Marked text is a normal intermediate editing state. Preserve it and validate or transform at a defined commit boundary rather than destroying the input method's interaction.

exercise.brief: Build DemoCodeForm in a scratch target, verify raw-buffer rules and UTF-16 replacements, and write an editing/keyboard acceptance record.
steps: Try empty/whitespace name, code 01234, pasted letters, non-ASCII digits, and selected replacement.
Use replacingDemoText on A🙂B with NSRange(location: 1, length: 2) and replacement X; explain the units.
Add field-specific localized messages and persistent labels without changing raw-buffer ownership.
Test explicit Done on the number pad, hardware-keyboard submit, and narrow-width large-text error recovery.
Use a composition-capable keyboard and record whether edits preserve marked text/caret; compare this evidence with the active model's source normalization.
acceptance: 01234 remains a string with its leading zero.
The synthetic rule accepts exactly five ASCII digits and rejects other characters at submission.
Replacing the emoji yields AXB without corrupting surrounding text.
Done dismisses input without clearing the buffers, and invalid submission focuses a repairable field.
The record distinguishes model-rule checks from actual keyboard and composition observations.
exercise.solution:
The form should accept Demo Ada plus 01234, preserve that raw code, and show the synthetic success status. Five Arabic-Indic digits fail this explicitly ASCII-only demo rule even though other systems may legitimately accept them. That is why the active repository's isWholeNumber predicate must be described separately. Whitespace-only names remain editable but fail eligibility. An invalid submission keeps the buffers and selects the first field needing repair.

For A🙂B, the UTF-16 representation has four code units: A, the emoji's surrogate pair, and B. Replacing location 1, length 2 with X yields AXB. Deleting a selected range uses the same helper with an empty replacement. A conversion failure returns nil; the caller must choose a safe no-edit or diagnostic policy rather than force-unwrapping it.

Provide localized labels and an error that names which rule failed. Keep the explicit Done path because submitLabel cannot supply a missing number-pad Return key. Test composition and selection through the real input method; a pure string helper cannot certify that experience. The report should identify the keyboard, OS, width, text category, and observed outcome, while marking unexecuted device fixtures pending. No live data or client submission is part of this exercise.

lessons.title: App and scene lifecycle: iPad adaptation, multiple windows, and restoration
lessons.summary: Separate process, scene, window, controller, and draft lifetimes; audit the production app-delegate path against the demo's scene setup and current Apple requirements.
objectives: Assign process services, scene navigation, and draft ownership at the correct lifetime.
Distinguish orientation changes and window resizing from Android configuration recreation.
Describe actual configured iPhone/iPad support and current scene migration limits.
Choose scene restoration versus durable draft storage with account/version validation.
Design independent windows without global key-window or navigation assumptions.

sections.title: Process, scene, window, controller, and document are different owners
sections.html:
Android's Activity/task model gives useful vocabulary for independent UI surfaces, but do not map an iOS scene one-to-one to an Activity. The app process owns application-level services. A UIScene represents an instance of UI with its own lifecycle. A UIWindowScene hosts windows for that scene. A UIWindow presents a view-controller hierarchy. A controller owns a screen or container, while a document or draft may have a longer or shorter business lifetime than that screen. Each boundary answers a different ownership question.

A process can host multiple scene sessions, and two windows can show different selections while sharing an authenticated service. A scene can become inactive while another remains active. Scene disconnection does not necessarily mean the process ends or its session is permanently discarded; the system may reconnect it later. Conversely, keeping a scene identifier in memory does not preserve the underlying draft through process death. Design persistence separately from lifetime, as sessions 009 and 019 established.

Draw ownership before callbacks: process service → account-scoped repository; scene root → navigation path, modal presentation, focus requests; draft owner → editable document values. Put a selection on a global singleton only if the product intends every window to share it. UIKit and SwiftUI can coexist inside a scene, so a hosted SwiftUI view does not create another app process or automatically another window. Multiple windows amplify bugs already familiar from Android: stale global references, leaked editing state, and navigation applied to the wrong surface.

sections.title: Interpret scene phases and avoid assuming timely termination callbacks
sections.html:
A scene commonly moves among active, inactive, and background states. Inactive can occur for interruptions and transitions; it is not always a full background departure. In scene-based UIKit, scene delegate callbacks describe the scene's events, while UIApplicationDelegate retains process-level responsibilities such as launch and some application services. After adopting the scene lifecycle, corresponding app-delegate UI lifecycle callbacks are no longer the owner for per-scene transitions. Audit each responsibility instead of copying every old method into a new delegate mechanically.

SwiftUI exposes scenePhase through the environment. Reading it inside a scene's view hierarchy provides that scene context; reading it at the App level can aggregate scene state. Place pause/resume decisions where their intended lifetime is visible. A timer drawing one window can pause when that scene becomes inactive, but cancelling a shared account service whenever any scene backgrounds would disrupt another active window. Background execution allowances are separate platform contracts; they do not make an arbitrary async task run forever.

Save important draft data as edits occur or through a deliberate bounded checkpoint. Do not rely on applicationWillTerminate or a single transition callback being delivered before the system kills a suspended process. State restoration is also not a data-integrity journal. Mark unsaved state, encode only what is necessary, and choose durable storage according to sensitivity and account ownership. Session 025's security boundary matters: scene state and restoration activities should not casually contain patient information, authentication tokens, or full network response objects.

sections.title: Read a per-window SwiftUI root with small restoration state
sections.html:
This illustrative iOS 17+ scratch app keeps navigation-like selection at the scene level and stores only a synthetic selected ID. It does not implement durable document storage. Keep exactly one @main type in an actual target; type-checking the source is not building an app bundle.

import SwiftUI

@main
struct DemoScenesApp: App {
    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup {
            DemoSceneRoot()
        }
    }
}

struct DemoSceneRoot: View {
    @Environment(\.scenePhase) private var phase
    @SceneStorage("demo.selectedID.v1") private var selectedID = ""
    @State private var status = "Ready"

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            List {
                Button("Select demo A") { selectedID = "demo-A" }
                Button("Clear selection") { selectedID = "" }
                Text(selectedID.isEmpty ? "No demo selection" : selectedID)
                Text(status)
            }
            .navigationTitle("Demo window")
        }
        .onChange(of: phase) { _, newPhase in
            switch newPhase {
            case .active:
                status = "This scene is active"
            case .inactive:
                status = "This scene is inactive"
            case .background:
                status = "This scene is in the background"
            @unknown default:
                status = "An additional scene phase"
            }
        }
    }
}

WindowGroup describes a family of scene windows; the root's State belongs to its identity within each scene, rather than being an App-owned global selection. SceneStorage uses a named, system-managed scene restoration value. The v1 key suggests a schema boundary; it does not migrate data automatically. The initial Ready value remains until a change occurs, so do not rely on onChange alone for all initial setup. @unknown default handles future enum cases the SDK may add.

A restored selectedID must be checked against current available records and the current account before routing. This demo shows it as text only. A real root should fall back gracefully if the referenced record was removed or inaccessible. The storage wrapper is not a promise to save every edit immediately and is unsuitable as the sole store for a critical draft. Do not claim the sample enables every runtime's multiple-window UI merely because it contains WindowGroup.

sections.title: Adapt to the scene's size, not an assumed device rotation
sections.html:
UIKit ordinarily keeps the same controller hierarchy through interface-orientation and window-size changes. Android often recreates an Activity for configuration changes unless handled differently. Therefore an iOS orientation event is not an automatic new model, restored bundle, or cancelled feature. A draft should usually remain with its owner. SwiftUI view descriptions can be recomputed without resetting identity-associated state. Process death and deliberate flow replacement are different reset boundaries.

Size classes are coarse environment categories, while window geometry can change continuously within one category. On iPad, a narrow window, a wide window, and an external display can present different available sizes without changing the physical device orientation. Orientation of the interface also differs from UIDevice.orientation, which can include face-up or face-down states. Choose layout from the current container size and relevant traits; request orientation changes only through appropriate platform APIs and product requirements, not by assigning private device values.

Adaptive navigation may use a split presentation at wide widths and a compact stack when narrow. Preserve selection and route meaning as the presentation changes; avoid reconstructing the draft because a sidebar disappeared. Popovers require correct source anchors and can adapt into other presentation styles. Reevaluate hit targets, readable width, keyboard positioning, and error visibility in each configuration. iOS 26-era windowing and resize APIs add options, but they are not automatically available at the checkout's iOS 17 minimum. Use availability guards or a deliberate raised minimum, and do not confuse installed SDK support with supported deployment versions.

sections.title: Each window needs its own navigation and a shared-data policy
sections.html:
Scene sessions have stable persistent identifiers useful for associating restoration state, but that identifier is not a domain document ID. A window displaying draft A needs both a scene identity and an explicit draft identity. If two windows open the same draft, choose whether they share live edits, maintain independent tentative changes, or resolve conflicting commits. A shared observable object can mirror changes intentionally; accidental global editing state can silently overwrite another window's work.

Do not find the first connected scene or an arbitrary global key window to present an alert. connectedScenes is a collection of contexts, not a guarantee that the first element is the user's initiating window. Route presentation through the controller, coordinator, or scene root that received the action. Keep scene-specific focus and scroll requests there too. Process services can be injected into each root, while navigation state stays local. A UIKit scene delegate usually creates its window from the UIWindowScene supplied at connection rather than from a global screen.

Logout crosses these lifetimes. Clear or invalidate account-bound drafts, restoration routes, and caches in every relevant scene, and reject late async work for the previous account. Backgrounding one scene should not log out or cancel another arbitrarily. When a scene is disconnected, release UI subscriptions and scene-owned tasks according to the contract, while retaining durable documents in their proper repository if needed. An iPad target declaration is not evidence that these semantics were implemented or tested. Specify two-window fixtures before claiming multiwindow support for a feature.

sections.title: Restoration resumes an interaction; persistence protects the data
sections.html:
SwiftUI SceneStorage is intended for lightweight scene-associated values, and AppStorage uses app-level defaults for supported preference types. The same defaults key can therefore affect multiple windows. Neither wrapper alone provides a complete durable, sensitive document model. A typed NavigationStack path can be encoded explicitly when its route values are Codable, or a NavigationPath can offer a codable representation when all its elements support that representation. Encoding possibility is not a guarantee of valid routes on the next launch.

UIKit's scene state-restoration activity can identify a document or interaction to reconnect. Older view-controller restoration uses restoration identifiers and encode/decode hooks. These mechanisms have different lifecycles and should not be mixed by assuming the system reconstructs every service or dependency. Recreate dependencies through the normal application boundary, load the identified data, validate the account and schema, then present the surviving route. Restore presentation meaning rather than arbitrary controller pointers or captured closures.

Use a versioned envelope with a domain identifier, selected record ID, and the minimum necessary route state. Handle corrupt data, an unknown version, a deleted record, and an account mismatch by falling back to a safe root and explaining recovery when needed. A keyboard's exact frame and a stale scroll proxy are not durable restoration data. Do not automatically resubmit a network operation because a confirmation route was restored. Saving a draft and restoring its screen are related but separately testable acceptance criteria. Specialist storage migration, conflict resolution, and security review remain necessary for real health-related documents.

sections.title: Actual support, unfinished migration, and current Apple requirements
sections.html:
The inspected Tuist helpers configure iPhone and iPad destinations for both production and demos. The production main target declares iOS 17.0 in Project.swift; the booking demo declares iOS 18.2. Production's Zocdoc-Info.plist declares only portrait for iPhone and all four ordinary orientations for iPad. It sets UIDesignRequiresCompatibility = true and has no UIRequiresFullScreen key. The inspected QA plist separately sets UIRequiresFullScreen = false; those keys are not interchangeable. The demo has a scene manifest with multiple-scenes enabled and its entry uses WindowGroup. These are configuration/source facts, not executed launch, orientation, or two-window results.

Production AppDelegate still constructs and retains a window and forwards app-level lifecycle callbacks. Nearby comments describe a future UIWindowScene migration, while an AppLaunchRouter shares forwarding logic in preparation. This audit therefore does not claim production has completed scene adoption. Read current effective build settings and generated plists before a release decision, because this checkout contains legacy SPM and Tuist paths during migration. Configured iPad destinations do not prove responsive feature layouts, multiwindow editing correctness, Catalyst support, native macOS support, or visionOS support.

Apple's current scene-transition documentation states that beginning with iOS/iPadOS 27 and the listed companion platforms, apps built with the latest SDK must adopt the scene-based lifecycle or fail to launch. This requirement concerns scene adoption; supporting multiple simultaneous scenes is still a separate choice. Apple also documents UIRequiresFullScreen as deprecated beginning in iPadOS 26 and to be ignored in a future release. Do not name an unsupported removal release or claim an actual checkout launch failure without building it. The gap is a source-backed release-readiness concern for further verification, not a migration implemented by this course.

quiz.question: One window backgrounds while another remains active. Which ownership policy is sound?
options: Always cancel every shared account operation.
Pause scene-owned work according to that scene's policy and keep shared services governed by their own owners.
Treat the whole process as terminated.
quiz.explanation: Scene and process lifetimes differ. A shared service may still be needed by another active scene; only the relevant scene-owned work should follow that scene transition.

quiz.question: What does SceneStorage provide?
options: A guaranteed immediate durable store for a critical draft.
One global navigation value shared by every window.
Lightweight system-managed restoration state associated with a scene.
quiz.explanation: Scene restoration values help resume UI. Their saving lifecycle is system managed; durable documents, sensitive data, account checks, and migrations need separate policies.

quiz.question: Does Apple's required scene adoption imply every app must support multiple simultaneous windows?
options: No; adoption and multiple-scene support are separate decisions.
Yes; every app must open two windows at launch.
Only if its deployment minimum is iOS 17.
quiz.explanation: Current Apple guidance distinguishes required scene lifecycle adoption from encouraged but separately chosen multiple-scene support. SDK-linked launch policy is not the same as a deployment minimum.

exercise.brief: Design a scratch scene-owned draft experience and a restoration envelope, then audit the checkout's configured device support and migration evidence.
steps: Use DemoScenesApp as a reading/type-check reference, then create a separate target with a confirmed scene/multiple-window configuration for runtime practice.
Keep a separate selected record and navigation state per window; define whether actual draft data is shared.
Resize a window and rotate where supported; record whether model identity and editing state persist.
Define a versioned restoration payload and handle unknown version, missing record, and account mismatch.
Read production AppDelegate, target helpers, and both target plist contracts; distinguish their behavior and current Apple requirements.
acceptance: Window A's selection does not change B unless sharing is explicitly specified.
Resizing does not accidentally reconstruct the draft owner or clear input.
Restoring a deleted or unauthorized record returns safely to a valid root.
Logout invalidates old account-bound restoration and late results across relevant windows.
The audit reports configuration facts and pending launch checks without claiming a completed scene migration.
exercise.solution:
The process owns a shared account service and repository. Each scene root owns its navigation path, sheet presentation, focus, and selected record. A durable draft is identified by domain ID and loaded from the appropriate account repository. If two windows intentionally share a draft, document synchronization and conflict behavior; otherwise give each edit session an independent tentative buffer and an explicit commit action.

A minimal restoration envelope can encode version 1, account-scope marker, draft ID, and an optional selected item ID. On restoration, first verify version and current account, then load the draft and resolve the selected item. Fall back to the list when the selected item no longer exists. Never store credentials in this envelope, and never treat decoding a route as authority to resubmit a request. SceneStorage can keep small UI selections while the repository protects the draft.

The checkout comparison should name production's app-delegate window construction and the demo's WindowGroup/scene manifest, iPhone/iPad configured destinations, production's portrait-phone/four-orientation-tablet plist, production's separate UIDesignRequiresCompatibility declaration, and QA's UIRequiresFullScreen = false. Add Apple's current SDK-linked scene adoption requirement as a separate verified policy. These facts identify what needs a release check; they do not show that a production launch or two-window test passed. Restoration and actual multiwindow interaction remain learner/specialist runtime work.

lessons.title: Integrated UI lab: a resilient draft, reusable picker, and scene review
lessons.summary: Build and review one synthetic UI flow with measurable layout, stable selection, raw editing, interoperable sizing, interruption behavior, and scene restoration contracts.
objectives: Connect sizing, identity, input, navigation, and lifecycle contracts in one scratch feature.
Define a finite fixture matrix and match each requirement to the smallest useful evidence.
Keep UIKit/SwiftUI interoperability inside a clear ownership and sizing boundary.
Reject stale page outcomes and validate restored selection without losing the current draft.
Write a source-backed review that separates implemented practice, verified results, and specialist gaps.

sections.title: Turn the introductory UI lab into a precise engineering contract
sections.html:
Session 013 built a synthetic draft, picker, and review. This lab adds the UI engineering requirements that a plausible first version misses. Create a separate learning target containing a display name, a five-ASCII-digit demo code, a provider picker, and a Review route. Use synthetic provider IDs and deliberately long labels. The picker must survive insertion and reordering, cancellation must preserve an existing committed choice, and invalid submission must explain what to repair. A UIKit label inside Review must size from the available width and update from current input.

Before implementing, name the product's minimum supported width, largest tested text category, and available orientations in the scratch target. Do not copy production's phone orientation declaration into your target without choosing it. If iPad multiple-window practice is included, specify independent selection/navigation per window and whether drafts themselves are shared. Scene restoration stores only minimal non-sensitive identifiers, while important draft values need an explicit durable policy if persistence is required.

Write a final-state contract for every action. Choose commits a provider ID and dismisses; Cancel dismisses without changing it; Review validates the current draft before appending its route; Reset clears the draft through an explicit action; resizing preserves its owner; a stale page cannot update a new query generation. A screenshot is useful only after those contracts exist. This is an engineering exercise using synthetic data, not a client feature migration, and the supplied solution remains a reference for your own pending implementation.

sections.title: Assign each source of truth before drawing controls
sections.html:
The scene root owns a draft model, a typed navigation path, and modal presentation. The model owns raw strings, the committed provider ID, and the current provider content store. A text field reads and writes the same raw buffer through a binding; a picker can keep a local tentative highlight if selection is confirmed later, but must not silently change the committed value during cancellation. Review reads the root's draft rather than seeding independent State copies from its current properties.

With Observation, a locally owned @Observable class can live in the root's @State. A receiving editor uses @Bindable when it needs projected property bindings. A read-only summary can receive a plain reference. Main-actor isolation protects UI-facing mutation, while a query revision protects relevance across await. Those annotations solve different problems. A parent retaining a model does not automatically retain the model's weak delegate; if your bridge uses one, draw the separate strong owner.

Label every lifetime: draft for the scene's editing session; modal for the current picker presentation; UIKit label for its representable identity; page request for its query generation; image interest for its resource consumer; focus for a unique field in the current hierarchy. Keep a scene-level route separate from business data. A restored provider ID must be reconciled against the current store, and logout must invalidate prior account data and late work. This ownership map makes a failure explainable before adding more wrappers or tasks.

sections.title: Build geometry in checkpoints and predict what can overflow
sections.html:
Checkpoint one is the editor with semantic fonts and persistent labels. Start at a narrow finite width and accessibility text rather than assuming a spacious default preview. A number-pad field has an explicit Done path. Error text wraps and remains reachable. Decide whether the field row should be horizontal or vertical when the label becomes long; raising every compression priority to required cannot recover missing space. Use the scrollable container to preserve access to the last action.

Checkpoint two is the provider picker. On UIKit, use reusable cells and stable diffable identifiers with an explicit reconfiguration policy. On SwiftUI, use List/ForEach with stable domain or occurrence IDs and keep heavy work out of body. Both variants must route selection by current identity, not an old index. A long provider subtitle may increase cell height. Estimated layout values should converge to actual content, while empty, loading, and additional-page failure states have distinct feedback.

Checkpoint three is Review's UIKit summary. A UIViewRepresentable updates its existing label and measures multiline content at the proposed width. A controller-based integration would additionally need full containment. Verify that the bridge does not publish a user-edit event during rendering and does not assume the screen width. Draw the padding/background wrapper order for its surrounding SwiftUI row. Try a narrower window after Review appears: the summary should remeasure instead of preserving an initial fixed height or rebuilding the entire draft to make layout work.

sections.title: Input and interruption are part of the feature, not finishing touches
sections.html:
Checkpoint four adds interaction policies. The editor has distinct focus cases and moves from name to code on submit. Invalid Review requests focus the first repairable field, while dismissing the keyboard preserves both strings. Test paste into a selected range and a leading-zero code. If you introduce normalization, preserve provisional input-method composition and selection. A pure String test cannot prove that a real keyboard, AutoFill, or hardware input behaves correctly.

The picker supports cancellation with no previous selection and with an existing choice. A programmatic dismissal, explicit Cancel button, and interactive sheet swipe should converge on the same cancellation semantics. If your design commits selection immediately, a highlighted row is already the committed value; if it uses Apply, keep the temporary highlight separate. Do not let an animation completion accidentally report a second result. A cancelled back gesture from Review should preserve the route and draft when the navigation container says the transition was cancelled.

Animate only transitions that communicate a requirement, and preserve the final result with reduced motion. A drag, if added for rearranging the fixture, needs a button or accessible action for the essential operation. Observe scroll requests inside the current reader, use stable targets, and decide whether new results should preserve the user's current viewport. Record actual accepted focus and visible content separately from focus requests and animation starts. These observations distinguish a correct state machine from a UI that merely looked correct at one moment.

sections.title: Create controlled asynchronous fixtures instead of relying on tapping speed
sections.html:
Checkpoint five is a synthetic page loader with explicit start and completion controls. Begin query A at generation 1, replace it with B at generation 2, complete B, then complete A. Run old success and old failure schedules. Both must leave B's presentation unchanged. Cancellation can reduce wasted work, but the generation check states ownership even if a fake ignores cancellation. Do not use a short sleep as evidence that the operation started; await the fake's start signal.

For paging, record the cursor being requested and prevent a second request for that same generation/cursor. Preserve already useful rows if a later page fails. A retry should request the failed page once and not discard the current selection. Declare how repeated IDs merge into the store and when an obsolete selected provider becomes unavailable. If selection is invalidated, explain the consequence in the UI rather than silently reviewing another provider at the same index.

The worked reference below covers synchronous fixture replacement and ID-safe selection. Adding the controlled loader is deliberate learner work using sessions 011 and 015, not a claim that the reference implements transport cancellation or production pagination. An image-completion fixture is separate: configure a cell for A, reuse it for B, then complete A's resource. The old result must not decorate B. These deterministic schedules provide stronger evidence than a hurried manual scroll, while real recognizer, keyboard, and layout interaction still needs a running target.

sections.title: Exercise resizing and restoration without inventing platform support
sections.html:
Checkpoint six places the root in a confirmed scene configuration. Resize where the runtime supports it, and rotate only where the scratch target declares the orientation. The root model should remain the same owner as geometry changes. SwiftUI may create new description values and UIKit may relayout existing views; neither observation implies Android-style Activity recreation. Record the available scene size, traits, and preserved draft rather than attributing every change to rotation.

For multiple windows, open A and B and choose different provider IDs. Changing A's local route or focus must not navigate B. If the application shares an account service, backgrounding A should not automatically cancel B's required work. Restoration should encode minimal route/selection meaning in a versioned envelope, then validate the current account and provider availability before presenting it. A removed provider falls back to the picker; an unknown schema falls back to a safe root. Restoring a screen must not repeat a submission.

The active checkout offers a SwiftUI WindowGroup demo and an app-delegate-owned production window. Compare them before claiming your lab matches production scene behavior. iPhone/iPad destinations, each plist's distinct compatibility declarations, and orientation declarations are configured support evidence, not runtime feature-quality evidence. Apple now requires scene adoption for the documented latest-SDK/iOS 27 launch case, while multiple simultaneous scenes remain a separate choice. This lab prepares a review of those boundaries; it does not change the app's lifecycle or release configuration.

sections.title: Use a small matrix of evidence rather than one giant UI test
sections.html:
Choose fixtures by risk. Pure validation tests cover whitespace names, five ASCII digits, leading zero preservation, missing selection, Reset, duplicate IDs, and generation rejection. Pure layout math can cover spacing, wrap positions, empty input, and overflow policy. A snapshot captures long labels and errors at chosen width, text category, appearance, and locale. UI automation or a documented manual run covers sheet cancellation, keyboard progression, an actual selected replacement, and a restored scene. Each layer proves a different boundary.

RequirementSmallest useful evidenceWhat it does not prove
Moved provider selects the same IDControlled reorder plus ID-result assertionReal gesture arbitration
Long error remains reachableLarge-text narrow-width rendering and scroll interactionIME composition
Old page cannot overwrite BControlled start/completion scheduleTransport cancellation
Window selection is independentTwo-window runtime sequenceDurable draft integrity after a crash

Record executed evidence with toolchain/SDK, deployment minimum, runtime/device, fixture, and result. A declaration in a test file is planned coverage until run. The repository's standard snapshot helper fixes particular dimensions and traits; it does not exhaust larger text, RTL, tablet, or dark mode. Do not re-record baselines to conceal a misunderstood diff. Keep performance numbers out of the report unless a measurement actually occurred; an apparently smooth simulator interaction is not a frame-distribution benchmark.

sections.title: Review the causal chain and preserve specialist boundaries
sections.html:
Finish with one user journey: type a demo name and code, choose A, replace/reorder providers, review, return, cancel another picker, resize, then restore. Explain which owner changes at each step and which identities persist. Use the active address model, carousel, custom layout, and demo app as source comparisons. The carousel is gated alongside a legacy branch; the address form has local US-centric constraints; the flow layout allows oversize children; the production scene migration is not complete in the inspected path. Those facts keep the comparison honest.

A useful finding names a trigger, violated contract, consequence, and evidence. For example, if a callback captures position zero, inserting C before A makes selecting the old A callback resolve C. The fix is identity-based selection, verified with a controlled reorder. If a summary has a fixed 44-point height, increasing text can clip it; the fix requires width-aware measurement and a large-text fixture, not a claim that all fixed sizes are wrong. If restored selection bypasses account checks, propose envelope validation before routing.

The remaining specialist work should be concrete: real IME and bidirectional editing, VoiceOver and alternative-input sessions, sophisticated custom-layout baselines/caching, iPad pointer and multiwindow conflict semantics, production scene migration, and representative-device profiling. These are further study or pending runtime evidence rather than completed course coverage. Your final review separates taught contracts, your practiced implementation, source-observed behavior, and executed checks. That distinction is the staff-level skill this lab develops alongside the code.

quiz.question: After provider A moves from index 0 to index 2, what should Review display?
options: Whatever currently occupies index 0.
The provider resolved by the committed ID A, or an explicit unavailable state if A was removed.
A fresh random provider ID.
quiz.explanation: Business selection belongs to identity, not position. Reordering preserves the selection; removal needs an explicit reconciliation policy rather than silently selecting another record.

quiz.question: Which check establishes obsolete page failure cannot clear query B?
options: A screenshot of B before A completes.
Annotating the model @MainActor.
Complete B, then complete A with an error under a controlled generation fixture and assert B remains.
quiz.explanation: A controlled old-error schedule exercises the catch-path freshness contract. Isolation and an earlier screenshot do not prove the post-await outcome.

quiz.question: A standard phone snapshot passes. Which conclusion is justified?
options: The configured fixture matched its baseline; keyboard, large text, and two-window behavior need their own evidence.
Every iPad layout and all input methods are correct.
Scene migration is complete.
quiz.explanation: A snapshot certifies its configured rendered state. It does not execute keyboard composition, scene reconnection, multiwindow ownership, or every environment.

Selection survives insertion/reorder by ID, and Cancel preserves the committed choice.

exercise.solution:
The following synchronous reference covers the owner, raw-buffer validation, stable selection, typed review route, cancellation, and width-aware UIKit summary. It is a scratch module, not production code. The provider replacement button supplies a deterministic reorder/insertion fixture. Add your controlled async page owner and restoration envelope as separate checkpoints; this reference intentionally does not claim those are implemented.

import Foundation
import Observation
import SwiftUI
import UIKit

struct LabProvider: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let name: String
}

enum LabRoute: Hashable { case review }

@MainActor
@Observable
final class LabDraft {
    var name = ""
    var code = ""
    var selectedID: String?
    var providers = [
        LabProvider(id: "A", name: "Demo Alpha with a long descriptive name"),
        LabProvider(id: "B", name: "Demo Beta")
    ]

    var selectedProvider: LabProvider? {
        providers.first { $0.id == selectedID }
    }
    var validName: Bool {
        !name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty
    }
    var validCode: Bool {
        code.utf8.count == 5 && code.utf8.allSatisfy { $0 >= 48 && $0 <= 57 }
    }
    var canReview: Bool {
        validName && validCode && selectedProvider != nil
    }

    func reset() {
        name = ""
        code = ""
        selectedID = nil
    }
}

@MainActor
struct LabRoot: View {
    enum Field: Hashable { case name, code }
    @State private var draft = LabDraft()
    @State private var path: [LabRoute] = []
    @State private var showsPicker = false
    @State private var attempted = false
    @FocusState private var focused: Field?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack(path: $path) {
            Form {
                Section("Synthetic draft") {
                    TextField("Demo name", text: $draft.name)
                        .focused($focused, equals: .name)
                        .submitLabel(.next)
                        .onSubmit { focused = .code }
                    TextField("Five ASCII digits", text: $draft.code)
                        .keyboardType(.numberPad)
                        .focused($focused, equals: .code)
                    Button(draft.selectedProvider?.name ?? "Choose demo provider") {
                        focused = nil
                        showsPicker = true
                    }
                }
                if attempted && !draft.canReview {
                    Text("Enter a name, five ASCII digits, and an available provider.")
                        .foregroundStyle(.red)
                }
                Button("Review") {
                    attempted = true
                    guard draft.canReview else {
                        focused = !draft.validName ? .name
                            : (!draft.validCode ? .code : nil)
                        return
                    }
                    focused = nil
                    path.append(.review)
                }
                Button("Reorder synthetic providers") {
                    withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .default) {
                        draft.providers = [
                            LabProvider(id: "C", name: "Demo Gamma"),
                            LabProvider(id: "B", name: "Demo Beta updated"),
                            LabProvider(id: "A", name: "Demo Alpha updated")
                        ]
                    }
                }
                Button("Reset draft") {
                    draft.reset()
                    attempted = false
                    focused = nil
                }
            }
            .navigationTitle("UI lab")
            .navigationDestination(for: LabRoute.self) { _ in
                LabReview(draft: draft)
            }
            .toolbar {
                ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .keyboard) {
                    Spacer()
                    Button("Done") { focused = nil }
                }
            }
            .sheet(isPresented: $showsPicker) {
                LabPicker(draft: draft)
            }
        }
    }
}

@MainActor
struct LabPicker: View {
    let draft: LabDraft
    @Environment(\.dismiss) private var dismiss

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            List(draft.providers) { provider in
                Button(provider.name) {
                    draft.selectedID = provider.id
                    dismiss()
                }
            }
            .navigationTitle("Synthetic providers")
            .toolbar {
                Button("Cancel") { dismiss() }
            }
        }
    }
}

@MainActor
struct LabReview: View {
    let draft: LabDraft

    var body: some View {
        Form {
            LabUIKitSummary(message:
                "\(draft.name) — \(draft.code) — \(draft.selectedProvider?.name ?? "Unavailable")")
            Text("Synthetic review only; no request was sent.")
        }
        .navigationTitle("Review")
    }
}

@MainActor
struct LabUIKitSummary: UIViewRepresentable {
    let message: String

    func makeUIView(context: Context) -> UILabel {
        let label = UILabel()
        label.numberOfLines = 0
        label.font = .preferredFont(forTextStyle: .body)
        label.adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory = true
        return label
    }

    func updateUIView(_ label: UILabel, context: Context) {
        if label.text != message {
            label.text = message
        }
    }

    func sizeThatFits(_ proposal: ProposedViewSize, uiView: UILabel, context: Context) -> CGSize? {
        guard let width = proposal.width, width.isFinite else { return nil }
        let boundedWidth = max(0, width)
        let measured = uiView.sizeThatFits(
            CGSize(width: boundedWidth, height: CGFloat.greatestFiniteMagnitude)
        )
        return CGSize(width: boundedWidth, height: measured.height)
    }
}

LabDraft owns the editable buffers and selection. selectedProvider derives the current content by ID instead of persisting an index. canReview combines format validity with the existence of that selection. Reset changes fields explicitly; it does not replace the model's identity or randomly rebuild navigation. @State preserves the locally created observable instance, while the projections used by TextField connect to its actual stored properties. The optional focus enum selects one field at a time.

NavigationStack binds a typed path; appending review creates the destination after current validation. The destination receives the same model. The picker commits only in its selection button. Cancel and an ordinary interactive dismissal do not modify the selection, so a previous choice remains. An Apply-style picker would need separate tentative state instead. The reorder fixture produces [C, B, A], and selecting A remains A even though its position changes.

The bridge creates one UIKit label per represented identity, applies current content in updateUIView, and measures against a finite proposed width. Returning nil for unspecified/unbounded width delegates to the default bridge strategy. The width contract and font scaling still need actual rendering evidence; compilation alone cannot certify line wrapping. A UILabel is a view, so this representable needs no child-controller containment. Replacing it with a hosted controller would reintroduce the session 008 containment contract.

For controlled paging, give the loader an injectable async operation and explicit start signal. Save generation and cursor before await, check both after completion, and apply only to the current owner. Perform the same guard in catch. Test B completing before A and A failing after B; neither may change B. Clear the in-flight cursor only when it belongs to that request, so an old completion cannot unlock a newer load accidentally.

For restoration, decode a versioned non-sensitive identifier envelope, validate account scope, load current providers, then resolve the selected ID. Do not restore input focus or resubmit work automatically. Finally, write executed results separately from pending two-window, IME, VoiceOver, and representative-device checks. This reference provides a concrete reviewable design while leaving the learner's lab and production application untouched.
